lowRated.like: I find Figma incredibly valuable for sharing design work. Its ability to easily share links with customers makes it seamless to convey ideas during meetings. Additionally, Figma fosters continuous learning, allowing me to explore and acquire new skills as I engage with its extensive features. The platform also makes it effortless to find references, which is essential in refining my design projects and ensuring they meet high standards. Figma serves as an effective tool for website design, enabling me to create aesthetically pleasing and functional web layouts. This capability enhances my productivity and allows me to deliver quality outcomes in my projects consistently.

lowRated.like: It's very intuitive and easy to use. It allows you to create clickable prototypes that you can demo without needing to write any code. Users can easily collaborate (if you can get the permissions set up right), work on the same document at the same time, and have a conversation in the comments section.
lowRated.dislike:
The permissions structure is terrible. You can set users as "Team Administrator" but they still can't access or change permissions on individual files unless the file owner allows it. So, if you have a file owned by someone, and they leave the company or you are no longer able to contact them, you basically lose the whole file because even a "Team Administrator" can't change the permissions. If you use contractors, I would strongly recommend AGAINST using Figma for this reason. Ironically, I was trying to give a user permissions to edit a file, and I got an error "You don't have permission to do that. Contact your team administrator." I am the team administrator. I guess I contact myself?

Also, their support is terrible. Absolutely terrible. They offer zero real-time support options, even

lowRated.like: What stands out most is the Figma Community. Having instant access to thousands of open-source design systems, UI kits, wireframes, and icons massively accelerates prototyping and ideation. Instead of building common elements from scratch, you can adapt proven components and learn directly from how other top design teams structure their files.
lowRated.dislike: Large files with extensive component libraries and multiple complex artboards can cause noticeable lag and high browser memory usage. Even on high-end machines, canvas rendering can slow down or trigger browser tab crashes during heavy multi-user collaboration.

default.like: Figma is my favorite piece of software I've ever used and it is constantly being updated with massive feature releases and improvements. At its core, it's a game-changer in collaborative design and creating a single source of cloud-based truth. As a marketing-side designer, it has become my most used program. But what makes Figma truly special is the constant stream of improvements, whether that's their great AI features, Figma Motion, Figma Draw, shaders, plugins–it's capabilities are remarkable.
default.dislike: Maybe the only downside is how difficult it is to find/download the original image used as an image fill in a file.

default.like: Sharing a file for comment is frictionless — a link beats exported PNGs in chat every time. Components and libraries keep shared design assets consistent across projects. Being browser-based means nothing to install for a quick review, and collaborators can look at the same file at the same time.
default.dislike: For a light user the Pro seat is more than I need most months. The tool's depth means occasional users re-learn where things are each time. File organisation across many projects takes deliberate housekeeping or it turns into a pile.

default.like: What I like best about Figma is its intuitive interface and real-time collaboration features. It makes designing interfaces, creating prototypes, and sharing feedback with team members incredibly easy. I also appreciate its component-based design system, which helps maintain consistency across projects and makes it easier to manage design updates efficiently.
default.dislike: One area I think Figma could improve is its performance when working with large and complex design files. Sometimes, files with many components, pages, and interactions can become slower to navigate. I would also like to see more flexibility in advanced features and better access to certain design system capabilities without needing higher-tier plans.

default.like:
Figma lets me design a brand system once and have every campaign pull from it. No more hunting for the right file version. I can hand a marketer an editable file instead of a static export. They swap the headline; I keep the brand intact. The comment thread lives on the artboard. Feedback stops getting lost in email and lives where the work is.

Figma plugs into the tools I already run on, like Slack, Notion, Jira, Google Drive. For marketing, I can push assets out to the channels that need them without rebuilding artwork three times.
